statement_record.book: (a) A prop signature is (G, s, t) with G a set and s, t : G -> N giving each generator its in-arity and out-arity. (b) A G-labeling of a port graph (V, in, out, iota) is l : V -> G with s(l v) = in(v) and t(l v) = out(v) for every vertex. (c) Free(G) is the prop whose morphisms m -> n are the G-labeled (m,n)-port graphs, with composition and monoidal structure exactly those of PG, the labelings carried along.

statement_record.book: The free prop Free(G) on a prop signature (G, s, t) has this universal property: for any prop C, the prop functors Free(G) -> C are in one-to-one correspondence with the functions from G to the morphisms of C sending each generator g to a morphism s(g) -> t(g) of C.
statement_record.intree: Definition Valuation : Type := ∀ m n : nat, S m n → (⟦m⟧ ~{P}~> ⟦n⟧).  [existence] InterpF : FreeCat S ⟶ P with InterpF_Strict/InterpF_Symmetric and `fmap[InterpF] (T_gen g) = v m n g := eq_refl`.  [uniqueness] Theorem interp_unique : ∀ m n (t : Term S m n), fmap[G] t ≈ hom_cast (eq_sym (Hobj m)) (eq_sym (Hobj n)) (interp P S v t), for any G with SG : StrictMonoidalFunctor, HB : SymmetricStrict G SG, Hobj : ∀ n, G n = ⟦n⟧ and Hgen agreeing with v on generators; Corollary interp_unique2 turns this into agreement of any two such competitors.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same in substance — the book's bijection is delivered as its two halves: existence (a Valuation, i.e. exactly an arity-respecting function G -> Mor(C) since S m n is the type of generators of arity (m,n), yields the strict symmetric monoidal InterpF that extends it definitionally) and uniqueness (interp_unique pins ANY strict symmetric competitor agreeing with v on generators; interp_unique_from_one, Universal.v:710, synthesises the object family from the single datum G 1 = ⟦1⟧). Encoding-level differences to note, none of which weakens the book's claim on the book's own props: (i) the target carries two side conditions, HomEqProp P (a Prop reflection of P's hom-setoid equivalence, needed only to build InterpF) and ObjDecEq P (decidable object equality, powering axiom-free UIP in the uniqueness proof) — both hold automatically for props in the book's sense (objects N, set-valued homs) and are supplied in-tree by FreeCat_HomEqProp / FreeCat_ObjDecEq (Instance.v:109,117) and their Quotient_* analogues; (ii) 'prop functor' is spelled as Functor + StrictMonoidalFunctor + SymmetricStrict (the braid square, Universal.v:445) + the object family Hobj rather than a bundled class, because the library has no PROP-morphism class; (iii) the correspondence is stated as existence + uniqueness rather than packaged as an iso of hom-sets in Sets.

#[export] Program Instance Term_Setoid {m n : nat} : Setoid (Term S m n) := {| equiv := @TermEq S m n |}  — used as the homset of FreeCat (Free.v:81), so the morphisms of the free prop are exactly expressions quotiented by the prop axioms.

| TE_tens_id : forall (m n : nat), TermEq (T_tens (T_id m) (T_id n)) (T_id (m + n))  — with TE_braid_hex_left/TE_braid_hex_right (TermEq.v:216,240) decomposing block braids, this identifies the extra in-tree primitives with the book's generated forms.

statement_record.book: Given G with s, t : G -> N, the G-generated prop expressions e : m -> n are defined inductively: (i) id_0 : 0 -> 0, id_1 : 1 -> 1 and sigma : 2 -> 2 are expressions; (ii) each g in G is an expression g : s(g) -> t(g); (iii) if alpha : m -> n and beta : p -> q are expressions so is alpha + beta : m+p -> n+q; (iv) if alpha : m -> n and beta : n -> p are expressions so is alpha ; beta : m -> p. Expr(G) is the set of all such; (m,n) is the arity. Distinct expressions may denote the same morphism of Free(G), so morphisms of the free prop are expressions quotiented by the prop axioms.

Inductive TermEqW : forall {m n}, Term Σ m n → Term Σ m n → Prop := | TEW_termeq {m n} (s t : Term Σ m n) : TermEq Σ s t → TermEqW s t | TEW_ax {m n} (s t : Term Σ m n) : smt_eqs E m n s t → TermEqW s t | TEW_sym ... | TEW_trans ... | TEW_comp {m n p} (f f' : Term Σ n p) (g g' : Term Σ m n) : TermEqW f f' → TermEqW g g' → TermEqW (T_comp f g) (T_comp f' g') | TEW_tens {m1 n1 m2 n2} (f f' : Term Σ m1 n1) (g g' : Term Σ m2 n2) : TermEqW f f' → TermEqW g g' → TermEqW (T_tens f g) (T_tens f' g').
Definition EqSystem (S : Signature) : Type := ∀ m n : nat, Term S m n → Term S m n → Prop.   Record SMT : Type := { smt_sig : Signature; smt_eqs : EqSystem smt_sig }.

statement_record.book: A presentation (G, s, t, E) for a prop consists of a set G of generators, functions s, t : G -> N, and a set E contained in Expr(G) x Expr(G) of pairs of G-generated prop expressions whose two components have the same arity ('the equations', traditionally 'relations'). The prop presented by (G, s, t, E) is the prop whose morphisms are the elements of Expr(G) quotiented both by e1 = e2 for every (e1,e2) in E and by the axioms of symmetric strict monoidal categories.
statement_record.intree: Record SMT : Type := { smt_sig : Signature; smt_eqs : EqSystem smt_sig } with EqSystem (S : Signature) := ∀ m n : nat, Term S m n → Term S m n → Prop.  Inductive TermEqW := TEW_termeq (TermEq Σ s t → TermEqW s t) | TEW_ax (smt_eqs E m n s t → TermEqW s t) | TEW_sym | TEW_trans | TEW_comp | TEW_tens.  Definition PresentedCat : Category := @Quotient (FreeCat Σ) (fun m n => @TermEqW m n) TermEqW_Congruence.  Definition PresentedPROP : PROP := {| prop_cat := PresentedCat; prop_strict := Presented_Strict; prop_symmetric := Presented_Symmetric; ... |}.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same. The presentation data match field for field: smt_sig is the (G, s, t) of Definition 5.25 in indexed form and smt_eqs is E, with the book's arity side condition ('the two components of each pair have the same arity') built into EqSystem's type since both arguments live in Term S m n at the SAME m, n. TermEqW is precisely the double quotient the book asks for — the smallest congruence containing both the strict-SMC equations (TEW_termeq, embedding TermEq, which IS the symmetric strict monoidal axiom set) and the theory's equations (TEW_ax) — and the result is delivered not merely as a category but as a bundled PROP whose strictness fields are eq_refl. Presentational differences only: E is a Prop-valued arity-indexed relation family rather than a subset of a product set, and the book's 'rough' hedge (its own informal Definition header) is discharged in-tree by an actual construction.

statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: both sides of the comparison are constructed (FreeCat Σ / FreePROP Σ on one side, PresentedCat E / PresentedPROP E over an SMT with an uninhabited equation system on the other), the presented one is BY CONSTRUCTION a quotient of the free one, they share objects and morphism carriers, and the comparison prop functor PresentedProj exists and is the identity on both — but nothing asserts that the comparison is invertible when E has no axioms, which is exactly what the exercise asks.

gap: The exercise's comparison is never stated. (1) No lemma says TermEqW E s t <-> TermEq Σ s t for an axiom-free E (grep for '<->' across Construction/PROP/ returns only Tietze.v:397), hence nothing shows the quotient is trivial; (2) no isomorphism or equivalence between PresentedPROP of the axiom-free theory and FreePROP is asserted (grep '≅|Isomorphism|Equivalence' across Construction/PROP/ finds only structural and tensor-comparison isos); (3) the axiom-free SMT is formed in-tree exactly once, as `Local Definition scratch_smt : SMT := {| smt_sig := Empty_Sig; smt_eqs := fun _ _ _ _ => False |}` (Construction/PROP/Tietze.v:756), and only to test that ext_retract reduces — it is never compared with FreeCat. The nearest in-tree result, Theorem AddEqn_derivable_conservative (Construction/PROP/Tietze.v:395: 'TermEqW AddEqn u u' <-> TermEqW E u u'' when the added equation is derivable), covers adding a DERIVABLE equation to an arbitrary theory, not the empty-theory-versus-free comparison. Finally, the book's own 'subtle difference' hinges on Free(G) being defined via port graphs while the presented prop is expressions-modulo-axioms; that identification is itself absent in-tree (see the gap recorded for def5.25), so the in-tree pair is the two SYNTACTIC constructions only.
